AI-assisted operational data point from a live `opencode web` incident; sharing sanitized structure only.

Environment:
- OpenCode `1.15.7`
- oh-my-openagent `4.3.0`
- `opencode web` / `prompt_async` path
- plugin source involved: `background-agent-parent-wake`

Observed persisted session shape:
- A synthetic/internal background completion reminder was persisted as a `role: user` message containing `<system-reminder>[BACKGROUND TASK COMPLETED]...` and `<!-- OMO_INTERNAL_INITIATOR -->`.
- That single internal user message became the parent of **51 assistant children** over ~507 seconds.
- Breakdown under that one parent: `finish: "tool-calls"` = 16, `finish: "stop"` = 35.
- Tools executed by the tool-call children included `read`, `bash`, `background_output`, `write`, `todowrite`, and `edit`.
- The first child started ~9ms after the internal reminder user message; subsequent children averaged ~10s apart.
- A later real user stop message also produced 5 assistant children under the same stop-message parent.

Why this seems relevant to #28202:
- This is not just visual duplication; the duplicate children are persisted backend session records.
- The triggering parent was not a real user instruction but a plugin-originated async parent wake (`background-agent-parent-wake`) delivered as a user-role internal prompt.
- The severity is higher than the 4-sibling examples: the same parent accumulated dozens of independent assistant turns, including tool-call turns that performed filesystem/shell actions.

Local code inspection matches the suspected path:
- OMO `ParentWakeNotifier.flushPendingParentWake()` dispatches `dispatchInternalPrompt({ mode: "async", source: "background-agent-parent-wake", ... parts: [createInternalAgentTextPart(notificationContent)] })`.
- The core invariant violation still appears to be OpenCode-side: overlapping async prompt traffic can create same-parent assistant siblings instead of preserving a single turn boundary.

This incident supports the fix direction in PR #28488: bind a runLoop to the initiating user turn and prevent concurrent/overlapping prompt traffic from writing terminal assistant siblings under the same parent.

One extra implementation detail that may be worth keeping explicit if this lands: the lazy-loading path should probably emit a small debug/telemetry receipt, not just save tokens.

The useful receipt shape I’d want while debugging a large MCP setup is roughly:

- startup: which MCP server/tool indexes were loaded up front, plus token/count buckets
- search: query hash/category, candidate tool ids, selected tool id, no raw query text required
- expansion: which full tool definition was expanded into context and why
- call: invoked server/tool id, argument/result redaction status, latency/status
- budget: before/after context-token buckets, so the saving is measurable per session/subagent

Reason: once tools are discovered on demand, failures become harder to explain: did the agent not find the tool, did it not load the definition, or did it load it but call it wrong? A privacy-safe receipt gives users maintainers can inspect without dumping tool args/results or private prompts.

I made a tiny executable fixture for this pattern here, in case it helps as a concrete reference rather than just prose: https://github.com/caioribeiroclw-pixel/pluribus/blob/main/examples/context-input-evidence/mcp-tool-search-otel-trace.json

Not suggesting opencode adopt that schema as-is — the main point is to keep “what was indexed/searched/expanded/called” observable as part of the feature.

I have the same issue with all Responses API endpoints - v1.15.7

When using models that route through the OpenAI Responses API (e.g. gpt-5.5 with provider openai), opencode fails with:

```text
ProviderShared.request: OpenAI Responses assistant messages only support text and tool-call content for now
```

I think that this happens because internal opencode scaffolding parts (reasoning, step-start, step-finish) present in assistant role messages are not being stripped before the request is sent to the Responses endpoint.

### Reproduction

Use a model that triggers the Responses path (e.g. openai/gpt-5.5)
Run a long agentic session with many tool calls and internal reasoning steps (common in tech-lead or complex multi-step tasks)

After some time, attempting to continue the session triggers the above error on the next assistant turn.

The session works fine with models that use the traditional Chat Completions path.

### Related

Similar message normalization work was done for Anthropic reasoning blocks in PR #23755 (src/provider/transform.ts).

Existing user demand for a Chat Completions fallback: #7793.

### Expected behavior

Internal opencode parts (reasoning, step-start, step-finish, etc.) should be filtered out for any provider/API path that only accepts text + tool-call content in assistant messages, with fallback to Chat Completions API if Responses throws an error. 

### OpenCode version

1.15.7

### Steps to reproduce

Use a model that triggers the Responses path (e.g. openai/gpt-5.5)
Run a long agentic session with many tool calls and internal reasoning steps (common in tech-lead or complex multi-step tasks)

After some time, attempting to continue the session triggers the above error on the next assistant turn.

The session works fine with models that use the traditional Chat Completions path.

## Update — scope of the bug is broader than just the `read` tool

Further testing during a workaround attempt confirmed the hang also affects the **`bash` tool when invoked through the agent's tool-call dispatcher**, but specifically when the command writes/creates artifacts (not just reads).

## Repro matrix (extended)

| Invocation path | Command | /mnt/c/ involved | Cross-FS write | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Direct `/session/<id>/shell` (e.g. wrapper's `opencode_shell_execute`) | `head -1 /mnt/c/.../file.md` | yes | no | ✅ ~10 ms |
| Direct `/session/<id>/shell` | `cat /mnt/c/.../file.md > /home/.../tmp.md` | yes | yes | ✅ ~13 ms |
| Direct `/session/<id>/shell` | `cp /mnt/c/.../file.md /home/.../tmp.md` | yes | yes | ✅ ~11 ms |
| Direct `/session/<id>/shell` | `mkdir -p /home/.../dir && cp /mnt/c/.../file.md /home/.../dir/ && ls -la /home/.../dir/` | yes | yes | ✅ ~15 ms |
| Agent tool-call (via `opencode_ask` → bash tool) | `head -1 /mnt/c/.../file.md` | yes | no | ✅ ~3 s |
| Agent tool-call (via `opencode_ask` → bash tool) | `mkdir -p /home/.../dir && cp /mnt/c/.../file.md /home/.../dir/ && ls -la /home/.../dir/` | yes | yes | ❌ hangs indefinitely |

So:

- **Direct shell execution** via the server's `/session/<id>/shell` endpoint works for all combinations, including `cp /mnt/c/ → /home/`.
- **Agent tool-call dispatch** works for read-only `/mnt/c/` access via the `bash` tool, but **hangs when the bash command writes to `/home/` while reading from `/mnt/c/`** (cross-filesystem write involving the project directory).
- Same hang signature as the `read` tool bug — `step=0 → service=llm ... stream → silence → no step=1` until manual `cancel`.

## Implication

The original report framed this as "the `read` tool hangs on `/mnt/...` paths". This update widens the surface: the actual root cause appears to sit in the **agent's tool-call dispatch / file-tracking layer**, not in any single tool implementation. The pattern that triggers the hang is:

> Tool call dispatched by the agent that involves a write (or modification) where one side of the operation is `/mnt/...` and the other is `/home/...` (or similar cross-DrvFs boundary).

Pure reads via the bash tool work. Pure direct-shell calls work. Only the agent-dispatched cross-FS write hangs.

## Plausible cause

Most likely culprit: the agent's per-tool-call **file change tracking** (the thing that powers `opencode_review_changes` / `session.diff`). If that layer uses `inotify` or a directory snapshot diff to detect what the tool modified, it may stall on cross-DrvFs writes:

- WSL2 `inotify` is reliable on the Linux native filesystem but unreliable / incomplete on DrvFs (the `/mnt/c/` mount layer).
- A snapshot diff that tries to stat both the source and destination across the DrvFs boundary may hang on a recursive stat() that doesn't return.

This would explain why direct shell (which presumably skips per-call change tracking) works, while agent-dispatched tool calls (which run change tracking after every tool invocation) hang.

## Updated workaround

For tasks that must move files from a Windows mount (`/mnt/c/...`) into the WSL project directory:

- **Do NOT** dispatch the cp via the agent (`opencode_ask`/`opencode_run`/`opencode_fire` asking the agent to run bash). Hangs.
- **DO** call the direct shell endpoint (e.g. `opencode_shell_execute` from the wrapper, which routes to `/session/<id>/shell` on the server). Works.
- Then dispatch the Phase 0 prompt with paths exclusively inside `/home/.../`. The agent's subsequent tool calls stay within the WSL native filesystem and don't trigger the hang.
